subject: ramenStall
pitch: A tiny ramen yatai at midnight: red noren curtain, steaming pot, three stools, paper lanterns swaying, a cat asleep under the counter, rain puddles reflecting the warm light. Studio Ghibli warmth: soft painted shapes, cozy lived-in clutter.
reasoning:
This is a big task—I'm planning a TypeScript module for a ramen yatai food cart stall, mostly static scenery, but thinking about whether to give the cat creature joints and add a swaying joint for lanterns, keeping the rig simple with a single root joint if I do.

I'll keep things static overall to reduce risk, maybe just tilting the lanterns slightly via part rotation rather than rigging joints. I'm mapping out the layout in meters: a roughly 2m wide, 1.2m deep wooden cart with a roof around 2.1m, customer-facing side with a noren curtain, counter, and stools, using primitives and paint/glow kits from the builder library for the construction.

Now I'm figuring out the wheel construction — placing two large spoked wheels at the cart's sides using torus geometry for the rim with boxes for spokes and a hub, getting the axis orientation right since torus defaults to a different axis than what I need.

Checking the tire sinks barely below floor, negligible. Now I'm working out the cart body dimensions - the wooden box frame, front counter panel, and overhanging countertop slab, thinking through how the yatai's open cooking interior should be laid out behind the counter.

I'll simplify to four corner posts supporting a roof, with a front counter panel, side panels, and a back shelf unit holding bowls and bottles, plus a stove and pot in the middle. I'm also considering placing the sleeping cat tucked under the cart itself.

Actually, simpler to skip a floating cart floor and make it a grounded stall instead: cabinets on short feet from y=0.12 to 0.95, with the central alcove open straight to the ground, and the cat curled up there on a little red cushion.

I'll shorten the shaft poles to keep the depth manageable, adding a small prop leg for support instead of a full stand. Then I'm placing three cylindrical wooden stools along the counter at evenly spaced positions, giving them a reasonable seat radius and height proportional to the counter's elevation.

For the roof, I'll build it as two sloped slabs meeting at a ridge, with eaves extending out as an overhang at the front, and paint on grain or stripe texture to suggest corrugated tin or wood paneling.

Working out the exact tilt angles and ridge/eave heights for the two roof slopes, then placing the noren curtain rod near the front eave above the counter.

I'm wary of relying on Japanese text rendering for the noren design, since CJK fonts might not be available — safer to draw a simple bowl-and-chopsticks icon instead of actual kanji characters.

Drawing each katakana stroke path...

Finishing the stroke paths for ン, then thinking about whether the noren should be a simple textured plane versus double-sided cards, since cards would let it read correctly when viewed from the flow direction, with the bottom edge anchored to the frame.

Realizing that hanging cards viewed from downstream display the drawing upside down (root edge on top) rather than mirrored, so I need to draw the SVG pre-flipped vertically to compensate.

This flip ambiguity is tricky, so I'll sidestep it entirely: instead model the noren as a thin box with the drawing texture mapped onto both front and back faces, since each face viewed from outside naturally shows the artwork unmirrored. The sides can just use a squeezed version of the texture since the box is only 12mm thick and mostly invisible.

For the rain puddles, I'll add small flat elliptical discs on the ground with a texture that blends a dark blue base with a warm reflected glow and streaks mimicking the lantern light, placing them only in a modest wet-stone patch beneath the stall since the brief names puddles but not a general ground.

Checking the min y stays within tolerance at -0.03, that works. I'm shaping the ground pad as an irregular blob extruded upward from an outline in the xz plane, centering its thickness around y=-0.015 so it sits flush with the floor.

Then I'm painting the top face with mottled wet-cobblestone colors, and adding flattened puddle shapes made from scaled circle geometry laid on top.

For the puddle texture, I'm designing an SVG with a cropped irregular blob showing a reflective indigo surface with warm lantern-light gradients, streaks, and subtle ripple rings, then giving the puddles a soft glow to sell the "reflecting light" effect.

For lighting fixtures, I'm planning paper lanterns (chochin) hanging at the roof's front corners around y≈1.75, red with ribbed stripes, plus maybe one white central lantern, built as a lathed bulb shape with painted rib detailing.

Designing the lantern texture...

Since actual lights might not export cleanly with the model, I'll skip real THREE.js lights and instead fake warm illumination by painting a glow onto nearby surfaces, writing a helper that blends base color toward a warm tone based on distance from lantern positions.

Defining light sources and paint logic...

I'm checking the paint texel density for a ~30m² stall area, landing around 6mm texels which should be fine for lighting cost. I also need to stay under the 64 flat-color limit, so I'll reserve flat colors for small parts and use paint for larger ones, watching that too many small painted parts don't bloat the atlas with extra charts.

Now I'm working out the stall's coordinate layout: counter dimensions, cabinet placement with doors and drawers, and the items sitting on the counter like bowls, chopstick holders, and a menu stand.

For the wood surfaces I'm planning to use a paint function with grain texture and plank seams along the y-axis, nested under lighting. Then I'm positioning the alcove back wall panel and the cushion where the cat sits underneath the counter.

Now I'm working out where to place the cooking elements on the countertop—deciding to put a large steaming stockpot on a small brazier-style stove toward the right side of the counter, near the back.

I'm also adding a second smaller pot with a bamboo ladle, and planning the steam effect as several soft, alpha-tested card sprites with gentle curves and lean, lightly glowed so they stay visible without being overpowering.

For the stove itself, I'm sizing the box and stockpot so they sit correctly on the counter—stove roughly 0.3 tall, pot 0.4 tall on top—then checking that rising steam near x=0.35, z=-0.15 tops out around 2.1, just under the roof's interior slope near the ridge so it doesn't clip through.

Actually I want to shrink the stove to a shorter brazier shape (0.22 tall) and adjust the pot dimensions so the steam tops out closer to 1.95, giving more clearance under the roof. I'm also laying out four corner posts for the structure, adding roof cross beams, and considering a back wall panel with a shelf of bottles to give the open-air kitchen more depth.

I'm thinking through adding a back wall plank with two shelves holding jars and bowls, plus hanging wooden menu tags with brushstroke-style marks and simple price text like "¥700" to make the stall feel authentic without needing real Japanese script rendering.

For the roof, I'm adding rafters and a dark fascia plank along the front eave, possibly with a small hanging sign above the noren and subtle painted trim details like gold dots or a scalloped pattern.

Now I'm working out the noren setup: a rod hung from two small hanger supports attached under the roof overhang, calculating the roofline's slope to position the hooks correctly, then laying out four cloth panels with even gaps, sized to hang from about chest height down to waist height.

Computing the sway geometry... I'll anchor each panel's top edge and rotate about the x-axis so the bottom swings outward in z while keeping the top fixed, using cosine/sine offsets scaled by half the panel height.

I'm now designing a generic hanging-part helper that applies Euler rotations and quaternions to position lantern geometry below an anchor point, then sizing the chochin lanterns (around 0.4 height, 0.17 belly radius) and planning rope attachments from the roof eaves, with two large red lanterns positioned at the front eave corners.

I'm working through placement math to avoid the lanterns overlapping the noren curtain -- adjusting x positions outward near the posts and considering small bracket arms extending from the posts to hang them cleanly in front.

For positioning, I'll hang them at ±1.05 under the roof eave edge, with a cord dropping the lantern body down so its center sits around y=1.8. I'm also adding a third, smaller bare-bulb lantern hanging centrally from the ridge above the counter for interior lighting.

For the lanterns, I'll go with two large red ones in front plus a small white/yellow one visible behind the noren slit, giving them slight opposing rotations (around 7° and -5°) so they read as mid-sway. Then I'm setting up three stools with splayed legs and round lathed seats, adding zabuton cushions to two of them for visual variety.

Assigning wood then paper-striped band then wood again for the umbrella shaft, skipping the handle hook detail for simplicity. Now I'm shifting to the cat, imagining a fat ginger tabby curled asleep on a cushion under the counter, with white belly and paws, built from a curved spine sweep.

For the cat's features, I'm planning a sphere head slightly scaled for shape, triangular/cone ears, and closed-eye details applied as a decal on the head surface using curved arc lines to suggest sleepy lashes. Mapping out the tail curve now, tracing its sweep from the hip through several angle points with decreasing radius toward the tip, checking it doesn't collide with where the head sits near the front of the body.

Now positioning the head itself, resting it near the end of the neck path with a low elevation as if lying on the front paws, and orienting its facing direction along the continuation of the body's curve.
